findings.title: `SDKExecutionSession.auto_memory` crashes when `base_options.env` is None
findings.description: The new property does `AUTO_MEMORY_DISABLE_ENV not in self.base_options.env`. `ClaudeAgentOptions.env` is an optional mapping (`dict[str, str] | None`), so on a session built with options that omit `env` this evaluates `... not in None` and raises `TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not iterable`. `SDKExecutionSession` is exported in `__all__` and is constructed directly — `tests/pipeline/conftest.py::scripted_session` builds it with `ClaudeAgentOptions(cwd=".", permission_mode="bypassPermissions")` (no `env`), and `dispatch.py:373` reads `session.auto_memory` on that surface. `open_pipeline_session` always sets a dict, so the production path is masked. The fix is `self.base_options.env or {}`. (The same optionality concern applies to `setting_sources` at lines 131–135: `list(sources)` yields `list[SettingSource]`, which is not assignable to the declared `list[str] | None` under strict pyright — the same Literal-vs-`str` mismatch the author already suppressed with `# pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]` at line 466.)

findings.title: `get_typed_config` accepts a bool for an `int`-typed key
findings.description: The `type_ is bool` branch guards the bool/int subclass relationship in one direction only. `type_ is int` still passes `isinstance(value, int)`, and `isinstance(True, int)` is `True`, so a hand-written `.squadron.toml` containing `pipeline.background_idle_timeout_s = true` is returned as `True` rather than rejected. `load_config` merges raw TOML values without coercing them to the declared type, so this is reachable without going through `set_config`. The concrete effect is `asyncio.timeout(True)` in `sdk_session.py:_background_idle_timeout_s` — a 1-second idle timeout where the operator asked for a number. The docstring promises the value is "validated against ``type_``"; the bool branch should be excluded from the int branch (`isinstance(value, bool)` → reject).

findings.title: No load test for the new background-wait / idle-timeout path
findings.description: The new dispatch path holds a live SDK session open while background agents run, with a configurable silence budget that defaults to 1800 s (`config/keys.py`, `pipeline.background_idle_timeout_s`), stops tracked tasks on expiry, and re-reads the stream across turns. This is exactly the "simulation, network, concurrency, or environment-layer" class the Python rules require a `tests/load/` tier for, asserting latency/throughput/resource bounds rather than functional correctness. The diff adds only unit tests against the fake `ScriptedClient` in `tests/pipeline/conftest.py` (with a 0.05 s synthetic timeout); no load test exercises a realistic configuration, so event-loop starvation, the 30-minute default bound, and the `stop_task` fan-out are untested at realistic scale. I could not confirm from the reviewed diff whether a `tests/load/` tier exists in this tree.

findings.title: Pipeline config is resolved against different directories for the session and the one-shot dispatch
findings.description: `open_pipeline_session` resolves `pipeline.user_settings`, `pipeline.auto_memory`, and `pipeline.background_idle_timeout_s` against `str(Path.cwd())` (the process cwd at session-open time), and `SDKExecutionSession._background_idle_timeout_s` re-reads against `base_options.cwd`. The one-shot path in `pipeline/actions/dispatch.py:141-150` resolves the same two keys against `cwd or "."`, i.e. the pipeline's `effective_cwd`. Today these coincide only because `run.py::_run_pipeline` never passes `cwd` to `execute_pipeline`; `execute_pipeline(cwd=...)` is a public parameter, so a caller that uses it would get one directory's `.squadron.toml` for the persistent session and another's for the one-shot dispatch — and the recorded `setting_sources` metadata would not describe the file that was actually read.

findings.title: The settings-policy docstring states an invariant the code does not enforce, and `sq serve` behavior changed silently
findings.description: The module docstring states that "no automated path may leave ``setting_sources`` unset", but `providers/sdk/provider.py:89-90` deliberately leaves the kwarg unset when `config.setting_sources is None` — the `sq serve` path — and `core/models.py` even carries a `SETTING_SOURCES_CLI_DEFAULT = "cli default"` sentinel for exactly that case. The docstring overstates the guarantee. Separately, the same provider change now always writes `kwargs["env"]`, and `AgentConfig.auto_memory` defaults to `False`; a `sq serve` agent therefore now receives `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1` where it previously received no env override at all. That is a real behavior change for a path the `pipeline.auto_memory` description does not mention ("pipeline sessions and pipeline dispatch only... Reviews, judges, PR, summary, and audit paths always run with memory off").

findings.title: The always-present digest lines change every review artifact's bytes
findings.description: The Run Digest now unconditionally emits `- System prompt:` and `- Settings sources:` lines, so every persisted review artifact — including clean passes — gains two lines. The same file documents a byte-identity constraint tied to a snapshot fixture ("the clean_pass_artifact.md snapshot guard depends on it", `persistence.py:293-299`). That fixture is a markdown file and the review scope excludes `*.md`, so I could not confirm whether it was regenerated in this change; it should be checked, since a stale fixture turns a passing suite red for a reason unrelated to the feature.
